record.hypothesis: The three-frame all-intra MP4 was changed from one-second to two-second sample durations by modifying timing tables and container durations only. The mdat is byte-identical. Chrome reports 6.0 s, shows red/green/blue for two seconds each, and reports only 3 total decoded video frames. This is a useful complement to R96: sparse/held presentations do not necessarily require a new video encode when the existing compressed samples already correspond to the desired visual states. R123: FFmpeg's normal Opus WebM had positive DiscardPadding=13,500,000 ns on the final block. Zeroing that metadata changed decoded output from 96,000 → 96,648 samples, exactly 648 samples = 13.5 ms at 48 kHz. Concatenated Opus packet payload SHA-256 stayed identical. Chrome plays both files and reports the same nominal 2.008 s container duration, so output trimming and HTML timeline metadata are separate observations.
